text:
sasha-support: Heads-up — multiple customers reporting 5xx / timeouts from hosted API (/v1/generate). Getting a spike of 502/504s. Example ids: req=01GZJ2-abc, req=01GZJ2-def. Logs show cache backend errors (Redis/memcached) around the same timestamps. Anyone on infra looking?

infra-bot: ALERT: cache-prefix-service error rate > 15% in us-west-2 between 16:02-16:06 UTC. Sample: 
`redis: connection error: EOF` 
`memcached: SERVER_ERROR out_of_memory`

maria-sre: I see the same in metrics — memcached p99 latency jumping and connection resets. Opening a session to the cache cluster now. Is there an ongoing deploy?

dave-ingest: No deploy on our side. We rolled a config tweak to prefix eviction policy last night (set cache.eviction-policy=volatile-lru) but that was a safe change. I'll double-check the rollout timeline.

ryan-engruntime: Repro steps from one customer: repeated streaming requests with long seq (context ~6k tokens) that create many unique prefixes. This may have increased memory pressure + kv key churn. Logs: 
```
ERR memcached: failed to store key=ctx:abcd... size=983040 flags=0: SERVER_ERROR out_of_memory
WARN prefix-cache: cache miss fallback to origin for key=ctx:abcd...
```

olivia-cs: Affected customers flagged support tickets: ACME Inc (prod), BrightApps (staging). ACME is seeing request failures in live traffic — raised as P1. Billing bot flagged potential double billing retries.

billing-bot: Notified: some retries may have generated duplicate usage events. Please avoid customer-visible retries until we confirm mitigation.

maria-sre: Immediate mitigation options: 
- 1) Toggle prefix cache to bypass (env var PREFIX_CACHE_ENABLED=false) on gateway for risky routes (/v1/generate) — cheap and fast. 
- 2) Increase cache autoscaler target or add nodes (slower). 
- 3) Short circuit long-context-heavy customers to a dedicated path that disables prefix caching.
Which route do we want?

sasha-support: Can we flip PREFIX_CACHE_ENABLED=false for hosted tier in us-west-2 for the next 30m? We need to stop customer impact and avoid billing duplicates. Patch must be coordinated with ops.

dave-ingest: I'll coordinate a quick config toggle on the gateway for us-west-2. Preparing a `svc-gateway` patch: 
```
kubectl set env deploy/gateway PREFIX_CACHE_ENABLED=false -n hosted-usw2
```
Rolling update will be 2-3 pods at a time. Expect reduced throughput but lower error surface.

maria-sre: Doing it now. Watching cache-err-rate and 5xx graphs.

infra-bot: Action: env change applied by dave-ingest at 16:11 UTC (rollout started).

maria-sre: Error rate dropping — memcached error logs tailing down, 5xxs decreased to baseline within ~90s. Confirming with a few synthetic requests.

ryan-engruntime: Thanks. We should also add a quick guard in runtime to detect memcached OOM and switch to direct origin for that request rather than retrying cache operations. I'll open a tiny PR.

olivia-cs: I messaged ACME and BrightApps that we applied an emergency mitigation (cache bypass) and are monitoring. They're asking for ETA on a permanent fix.

sasha-support: Good. Can we summarize root cause and next steps? I'll need a short note for affected customers.

maria-sre: Preliminary RCA: memcached cluster experienced memory pressure due to a sudden increase in unique prefix keys from a subset of long-context streaming workloads. This triggered server-side OOMs and connection failures. Contributing factors: high prefix TTLs (12h), cache eviction policy churn after config change, insufficient autoscaler headroom.

maria-sre: Short-term: keep PREFIX_CACHE_ENABLED=false in us-west-2 for 1 hour, add additional memcached nodes as a safety buffer, lower default prefix TTL to 1h, and add runtime fallback to skip cache on memcached OOM for individual requests.

dave-ingest: I'll add a conservative autoscaler bump and reduce default TTL. 

ryan-engruntime: PR opened for runtime guard and a metrics signal (memcached-server-ooms > 0 triggers automatic per-route cache bypass).

olivia-cs: I'll update customers: applied emergency bypass, root cause under investigation, next update in 2 hours.

billing-bot: Found ~120 duplicate usage events from retry storms; holding billing adjustments. Finance notified.

maria-sre: After autoscaler and TTL change, we're starting to re-enable prefix cache with a staged rollout and per-route opt-in. Reenable plan: enable for low-risk routes first, monitor memcached OOMs for 15m windows.

infra-bot: NOTE: memcached cluster stabilized at 16:42 UTC. No further OOMs observed in the last 10 minutes.

sasha-support: Thanks team. I'll keep this thread open until all customers confirm recovery and CS has had time to follow up. Please add postmortem when done.

olivia-cs: ACME confirmed recovery at 16:50 UTC. BrightApps OK at 16:52 UTC.

maria-sre: Postmortem checklist created: ops action log, metric screenshots, PR links: runtime guard, autoscaler change, TTL config change. Assigning owner: maria-sre.

sasha-support: Closing the immediate escalation. Filing follow-up: reduce default prefix TTL across regions, add per-customer cache usage limits, and billing reconciliation for duplicates.

sasha-support: Closing thread — will paste postmortem link once ready. :white_check_mark:
